blocking_issues.location_en: Structural-indicator table; section 'The country is a major external creditor even when trade is not consistently in surplus'; IIP chart; Sources and limitations.
blocking_issues.location_pt_BR: Tabela de indicadores estruturais; seção 'O país é grande credor externo mesmo quando o comércio não está sempre em superávit'; gráfico da posição internacional de investimentos; Fontes e limitações.
blocking_issues.issue: The rework correctly moved the IIP anchor from end-2025 to end-March 2026, but it still presents end-March 2026 as the latest reference. The Ministry of Finance IIP index shows that an end-June 2026 preliminary quarterly estimate was released on September 8, 2026, and that the end-March estimate was revised on the same date. Because the dossier is dated September 18 and explicitly labels the IIP row as the latest reference, the central external-balance evidence remains temporally stale and also uses the preliminary March vintage after a revised March estimate became available.
evidence: Japan Ministry of Finance, International Investment Position index: https://www.mof.go.jp/english/policy/international_policy/reference/iip/index.htm — end-June 2026 preliminary estimate released September 8, 2026; end-March 2026 revised estimate released September 8, 2026.

required_fixes: Update the structural-indicator table, external-balance discussion and IIP chart in both languages to the end-June 2026 preliminary IIP released September 8, 2026, if the field continues to claim 'Latest reference' / 'Referência mais recente'.

If March 2026 is analytically retained for a specific comparison, remove the latest-reference framing, use the September 8 revised March vintage rather than the superseded preliminary vintage, and explain why March is the appropriate comparison point.
Keep EN/PT-BR values, units, period/status labels, visual data and interpretation semantically identical after correction. Preserve the dossier identity, related_research_ids and controlled taxonomy.

country_context_contract.summary: Country-level Japan dossier with canonical related research IDs and a material reusable connection to BOJ normalization, global bond transmission, demography and energy-import exposure.

taxonomy.summary: Program, related programs, dimensions, geography, topics, cadence and demographic-transition phenomenon are consistent with the controlled architecture.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Direct analytical opening, informative headings, natural EN/PT-BR localization, coherent progression and no material template/meta-QA leakage were found in the reviewed editions.

contextual_depth.summary: Political institutions, BOJ independence, demographic constraints, fiscal transmission, external-creditor structure, energy dependence and industrial policy are connected through mechanisms rather than ornamental context.

visual_evidence_readiness.summary: The country-dossier visual floor is exceeded and EN/PT-BR structure is parallel, but the central IIP chart uses a superseded March preliminary vintage and is framed as current despite a June 2026 preliminary estimate being available before publication date.

translation.summary: The two editions are semantically aligned in the reviewed material; the IIP correction must be applied symmetrically.

contrary_evidence: The Ministry of Finance release calendar directly contradicts the report's latest-reference framing: end-June 2026 preliminary IIP was available on September 8, ten days before the dossier date, and the March estimate had also been revised.
limitations: This rejection is narrowly blocking on the current-vintage IIP anchor; it does not overturn the structural conclusion that Japan is a large net external creditor.
Several energy indicators intentionally refer to FY2023 and are explicitly labeled as structural reference points rather than current-month observations.

The September 18 BOJ policy rate of 1.25% was corroborated by contemporaneous reporting; transmission from normalization into portfolio allocation remains inferential rather than an observed automatic repatriation mechanism.
